title: ERP orders contract, checked against the deliveries
subtitle: Does contracts/erp.yaml (v0.3) describe what the ERP team really sends, before sign-off?

verdict.text: No. It holds on format, key, code lists and frequency, but it is wrong about `amount` (decimal currency units, not integer cents, and a decimal comma since 3 Nov), about `sales_rep_code` (dropped on 4 Nov) and about the delivery time (07:06–07:37 every working day, not 06:00). The amount breaks loads first: `silver.orders` failed on every delivery from 3 Nov, and `gold.sales_daily` was not rebuilt after that.

items.title: `amount` is decimal currency units, not integer cents, and has a decimal comma since 3 Nov; silver.orders fails on it
items.evidence: All 2,452 amounts in the three deliveries break `integer (cents)`: 2 Nov 401 of 401 shaped `9.99`, 3 Nov 1,038 of 1,038 and 4 Nov 1,013 of 1,013 shaped `9,99`, quoted because they hold the delimiter. No thousands separator in any of them. Our code already reads the column as units: `cast(amount as numeric(12, 2))` at silver/orders.sql:18, with no division by 100 anywhere, so the `cents` clause matches neither the data nor the loader. The comma broke that cast: `silver.orders` failed on 3 Nov (twice) and 4 Nov with `invalid input syntax for type numeric: "18846,00"`, and `build_sales_daily` was skipped both days (runs.jsonl:322, 336). As of the last run record (4 Nov), `gold.sales_daily` has no orders dated 2 or 3 Nov. This is the same change the ERP vendor update made to invoices on 14 Sep; that incident's open item, "check the other ERP amount columns" (ops/incident-log.md:13), was this column.
items.fix: Contract: `type: decimal`, `scale: 2`, `unit: units of currency`, `decimal_separator: ","` from 3 Nov, `thousands_separator: none`, confirmed with the ERP owner (Q4, Q5). Loader (ours, after your yes): silver/orders.sql:18 → `util.parse_amount(amount)`, as silver/invoices.sql:11 does. Then rerun `load_erp_orders` for 3 and 4 Nov and `build_sales_daily` after it (docs/howto/rerun-a-failed-job.md:8).

items.title: Working-day deliveries never arrive by `deliver_by: 06:00`
items.evidence: 23 of 31 orders files (5 Oct–4 Nov) arrived after 06:00, between 07:06 and 07:37: median 80 minutes late, at most 97. They were late on every working day (Mon 5, Tue 5, Wed 5, Thu 4, Fri 4) and on time on all 8 weekend days (05:38–05:47), so the ERP's working-day export runs after the promised time. Nothing has broken yet because `load_erp_orders` starts at 06:30 and waits up to 180 minutes (commit 3e47102). `gold.sales_daily` still started as late as 07:44 (runs.jsonl:5, 5 Oct), and finance reads it at 08:00.
items.fix: Agree one of two things with the ERP owner (Q3): they move the working-day export so it lands before 06:00 (or 07:00), or the contract says what they can hold. The proposal below uses 07:45, 8 minutes after the latest arrival seen. At 07:45 the 08:00 finance read has little slack; take that up with finance.

items.title: `sales_rep_code` dropped from the 4 Nov delivery, unannounced
items.evidence: Present on 2 and 3 Nov, missing from 4 Nov (1 of 3 deliveries, the latest). The bronze load succeeded because the loader inserts only the delivered columns, so `bronze.erp_orders.sales_rep_code` is null from 4 Nov. `silver.orders` and `gold.sales_daily` do not select it, and no job, SQL or check in the repo reads it. Nothing breaks today, but the contract promises a column that is no longer sent.
items.fix: Ask the ERP owner whether it is gone for good (Q6). If it is, remove it from the contract, as proposed below. If it was a mistake, they restore it and the column stays.

items.title: No owner and no change process: two unannounced changes in three deliveries
items.evidence: `owner: TBD`, `change_process: TBD`. The registry names only a team (`owner_team: ERP team`). The decimal comma (3 Nov) and the dropped column (4 Nov) both reached us without notice. The first one stopped silver.
items.fix: A named owner at the ERP team (Q1) and a notice period that covers ERP vendor updates (Q2); proposal below.

items.title: Ours, not the ERP's: the `amount > 0` rule has no working check
items.evidence: The data holds the rule today: 0 of 2,452 amounts are zero or negative. The check that should enforce it queries `amount < amount`, which is never true, so a zero or negative amount would pass.
items.fix: Platform side: change the condition to `amount <= 0`. Not a question for the ERP team.

sections.title: The contract to agree
sections.intro: Version 0.3 with every fix applied. Comments mark changed and new clauses and point to the questions below. Nothing is written to the repository until you say yes.

blocks.code:
# Data contract: the ERP orders delivery, between the ERP team and the data platform.
# The invoices, returns and payments files will get their own sections once this one is agreed.
contract: erp_orders
version: "0.4"                      # CHANGED: was 0.3
source: erp
dataset: orders
owner: "ERP team: <name, e-mail>"   # CHANGED: was TBD. Q1
change_process:                     # CHANGED: was TBD. Q2
  notice: 10 working days before the change ships
  covers: columns, types, number and date formats, delimiter, encoding, delivery time, ERP vendor updates
  announce_to: data platform team
  agreed_by: the owners of both sides, in writing
delivery:
  path: "sources/erp/{date}/orders.csv"
  content: the order lines of the previous day
  format: csv
  delimiter: ","
  quote: '"'                        # NEW: a value holding the delimiter is quoted (every amount since 3 Nov)
  encoding: utf-8
  header: true
  frequency: daily
  deliver_by: "07:45"               # CHANGED: was 06:00; Mon-Fri arrived 07:06-07:37, Sat-Sun 05:38-05:47. Q3
  timezone: Europe/Belgrade
key:
  - order_id
  - line_no
columns:
  - name: order_id
    type: string
    required: true
  - name: line_no
    type: integer
    required: true
  - name: order_date
    type: date
    format: YYYY-MM-DD
    required: true
  - name: store_id
    type: string
    required: true
  - name: customer_id
    type: string
    required: true
  - name: product_id
    type: string
    required: true
  - name: quantity
    type: integer
  - name: weight_g
    type: integer
  - name: amount
    type: decimal                   # CHANGED: was integer; every delivered value has two decimals
    scale: 2                        # NEW
    unit: units of currency         # CHANGED: was cents. Q5
    decimal_separator: ","          # NEW: comma since the delivery of 3 Nov, point on 2 Nov. Q4
    thousands_separator: none       # NEW: none in 2,452 values. Q4
    required: true
  - name: currency
    type: string
    allowed: [RSD, EUR, HUF]
  - name: status
    type: string
    allowed: [delivered, cancelled, on_hold]
  # REMOVED: sales_rep_code, missing from the delivery of 4 Nov and read by no job. Q6
quality:
  - "order_id and line_no together are unique"
  - "amount > 0"
consumers:
  - bronze.erp_orders               # NEW: the landing table load_erp_orders writes
  - silver.orders
  - gold.sales_daily

items: Q1: Who at the ERP team owns the orders file and answers for it when it changes?
Q2: Will you announce changes to columns, number or date formats, or the delivery time 10 working days ahead, ERP vendor updates included?
Q3: On working days the file arrives 07:06–07:37 and on weekends before 05:47. Can the working-day export land by 06:00, or at least 07:00? If not, can you hold 07:45 every working day?

Q4: Is the decimal comma in `amount` since 3 Nov permanent, as it was for invoices after vendor update 2026.9? Will a thousands separator ever appear (invoices got one: `1.234,50`)? Could you send a decimal point instead?
Q5: Is `amount` always in units of `currency` with two decimals, never cents?
Q6: Was `sales_rep_code` removed on purpose on 4 Nov? Will it come back?

Q7 (outside the contract today): since 28 Oct, two store ids unknown to `ref.stores` hold 107–129 order lines a day in quarantine (109 of 401 on 2 Nov). Are these new stores, and can the ERP team announce new stores ahead?

sections.title: What this check did not cover

items: Only three orders files are kept on this host (2–4 Nov; deliveries are git-ignored and ops files are kept 31 days). The amount format before 2 Nov is not checked, so I can't say whether `cents` ever held [guess].
The delivery log and run records end on 4 Nov. Whether the 5–10 Nov deliveries loaded is not known from here.
There is no metadata document for the ERP files in the repo (`sources/crm/README-vendor.md` is the CRM's), so I made no document comparison.
The invoices, returns and payments files (contract line 2) were not checked.
`weight_g` is 0 at minimum in the 3 and 4 Nov files. The contract has no rule for it and I did not count those rows.
The unknown store ids in quarantine are our reference data (`ref/stores.csv`, unchanged since the first commit), not a contract clause.
Doc drift outside the contract: docs/runbook.md:11 says `load_erp_orders` runs at 05:00; the job runs at 06:30.
No row values were read or shown; columns and counts only.
